title: Landscape Architecture Design Studio I
requirements: For students of MSc in Landscape Architecture.
description: This first studio course trains students in Landscape Architecture design principles towards sustainable design, situating them in the language of the discipline by introducing them to contemporary landscape theories and discourses. Appropriately scaled design projects explore issues of context, programme, landscape forms and processes as well as landscape design representation. Studio-based teaching comprises regular coursework presentation in critical review sessions. Field trips allow students to gain first-hand experience in encountering landscape designs in-situ. This master-level course consolidates proficiency in landscape design skills, enabling students to master an iterative, reflective design process, and produce design propositions with reason, imagination and ecological sensitivity within limited time.
outcome: Develop complex landscape architectural propositions that strategically apply Nature-Based Solutions, with a rigorous understanding of the site's complex ecological, social, and policy contexts. Develop the ability to frame and pursue a design research inquiry that leads to an innovative strategic framework for intervention. Develop the communication skills related to the conceptual, spatial, and systemic aspects of landscape strategy through diagrams, strategic maps, reports, and verbal presentations. Develop a capacity for critical inquiry and collaborative exploration, using the design process to mediate and synthesize diverse disciplinary perspectives and stakeholder interests. Develop a rigorous design methodology that is grounded in the School’s commitment to placing Nature and People at the center of design, enabling the formulation of a critical and socially responsible design position.
syllabus: Part I: Project initiation and site analysis, conducted through joint workshops with project partners to define goals and constraints.Part II: Strategic framework development. Students will present iterative concepts to a panel of stakeholders for feedback, culminating in a comprehensive vision plan that is grounded in the realities of the project.
required_readings: Please refer to the course outline.

title: Landscape Architecture Design Studio II
requirements: For students of MSc in Landscape Architecture.
description: The second studio course expands the scale, scope and complexity of landscape design issues investigated. Design projects will encompass larger sites to address more complex urban-rural sustainable design issues. Students will improve their design skills to articulate more considered proposals in terms of design language, responses to site and project brief, socio-economic considerations and disciplinary understanding. There may be interaction with related planning issues and engineering technologies, as well as possible collaborative learning with related disciplines such as architecture and urban design. Students will learn to develop innovative proposals using sustainable and ecological design principles.
outcome: Articulate and justify design decisions based on their social and ecological impacts, demonstrating a critical understanding of the landscape architect’s agency in prioritizing Nature and People. Develop the ability to advance a design project from strategic concept to detailed resolution through rigorous research, testing, and iterative refinement. Develop the communication skills related to the technical, spatial, and performative aspects of the design through detailed drawings, technical specifications, physical/digital models, and verbal communication. Develop the ability to critically integrate advanced technical knowledge from specialist consultants into a cohesive and resolved design proposal.
syllabus: Part I: Design development and systems integration, featuring technical workshops led by industry specialists.Part II: Detailed design and documentation. Students will prepare a final, comprehensive proposal for a formal presentation to the collaborating government agencies, developers, and stakeholders, demonstrating the project's tangible contributions.
required_readings: Please refer to the course outline.

title: Advanced Topics in Landscape Architecture
requirements: For students of MSc in Landscape Architecture, MSc in Urban Design and MArch.
description: This course examines emerging issues within landscape architecture, exploring its potential capacity to understand, critique and imagine our increasingly complex human-environmental systems in the face of contemporary global problems such as climate change, biodiversity, environmental and spatial injustice, etc. Through seminars, case studies and guest talks, this course interrogates current issues of landscape research, sustainable design and practice through selected themes - (e.g.. historic and cultural landscapes, border/edge conditions, urban-rural interfaces, land-water ecologies, etc.)

title: Topical Studies in Rural Revitalisation
requirements: For students of MSc in Landscape Architecture, MSc in Urban Design and MArch.
description: This course explores theories and ideas of landscape heritage, proactive conservation and holistic regeneration. Students will research and work on real‐life projects of rural revitalisation Hong Kong’s remote countryside, visiting actual sites and meeting villagers and stakeholders. Students will understand, experience and participate in the rural revitalization of Hong Kong’s eco‐cultural landscape. Students will 1) research rural conservation practices and policies local and abroad; 2) document, map and study landscape and fabric conditions; 3) develop sustainable design strategies and regenerative prototypes on site while consulting with villagers and experts from relevant disciplines.
outcome: Students will be able to: Research rural conservation practices and policies, both locally and abroad. Document, map, and study existing landscape and cultural fabric conditions. Develop sustainable design strategies and regenerative prototypes in consultation with villagers and interdisciplinary experts.
syllabus: The course is structured around a live rural revitalisation project. Coursework involves field research, site documentation and mapping, and the development of design strategies through direct consultation with community stakeholders and experts.
required_readings: Please refer to the course outline.

title: Computational Techniques in Landscape Design
requirements: For students of MSc in Landscape Architecture.
description: This course explores the latest advances in computational tools for landscape architecture that is able to document, analyse and simulate landscapes to high levels of precision through the generation of 3D digital models from various two-dimensional data accessible (ecological, social, topographical, etc). Students will be introduced to GIS spatial analysis, digital information modelling and simulations that relate to contemporary landscape design practice.

title: Landscape Technology and Construction
requirements: For students of MSc in Landscape Architecture.
description: This course consists of two parts. The first part explores how modern technology transforms perception, experience and understanding of built landscapes and natural environments, and covers relevant technological knowledge and skills in site analysis and planning. Geographic Information System (GIS) is provided as an essential tool for mapping, analysing, managing and modelling relevant landscape data. The second part focuses on landscape engineering aspects. Site engineering topics will include site investigation, earthworks, grading, drainage, basic surveying, etc., while principles and technologies of sustainable landscape design such as hydrology and hydraulics fundamentals, storm water management, bioretention systems and constructed wetland construction will be introduced.

title: Ecology and Planting in Landscape Design
requirements: For students of MSc in Landscape Architecture.
description: This course covers essential fundamental knowledge and skills for landscape practitioners in sustainable design regarding biophysical systems, ecology and horticulture, and their effective impacts on the design process. Ecological principles and concepts, impacts of land developments on urban ecology and ecosystem processes will be introduced. Key content will comprise vegetation types and habitats, a comprehensive understanding of plant species and plant communities in Hong Kong and Southern China, together with basic principles and vocabulary of plant identification, planting design and horticultural maintenance.
outcome: Students will be able to: Develop a macro understanding of ecology to analyze environmental systems and their interrelationships across scales. Apply this integrated understanding to design high-performance, Nature-Based Solutions and functional plant communities. Leverage ecological knowledge to frame and justify design interventions in economic terms.
syllabus: The course is structured as a series of modules, each led by a specialist. The syllabus combines lectures, field studies, and data analysis workshops..
required_readings: Please refer to the course outline.

title: Urban and Landscape History and Theory
requirements: For students of MSc in Landscape Architecture.
description: This course explores the history of urbanization and landscape and its theories, examining why and how cities and landscapes evolved with respect to their geographical and cultural contexts, while also considering more recent and contemporary cases of urban and landscape design that respond to more pressing ecological questions and more recent ecological frameworks such as the UN SDGs. The lectures are organized into themes that is roughly chronological, while focusing on topical issues to stimulate discussions and debates within the class.
outcome: This course will provide students with skills to understand complex forces that shape cities, and introduces critical methods and tools to describe and theorize the urban processes that influence the built environment. Using a themed approach and in-depth case studies, students will learn to articulate the relationship between visual and physical form of the urban environment and urban settings, processes and contexts in different perspectives, styles and methods of inquiry.
syllabus: This course examines the main ideas, histories and theories of the city through specific local and international examples from significant historical, political, geographical and environmental periods and aspects. Important themes and debates in urban design and planning will be critically explored to understand the relationship between the urban forms, the culture of cities and their sustainable development. In particular, the way urban forms have been used and reinterpreted, adapted and challenged by different social, economic and political contexts. Exemplary design projects and planning policies are investigated in view of their relationship to contexts and their impacts on communities and the environment.
required_readings: Please refer to the course outline.

title: Landscape Architecture Design Studio III
requirements: For students of MSc in Landscape Architecture.
description: The third studio course further develops students’ ability to research, analyse, conceptualise and create substantial landscape designs that articulate rigorous, organised and critical design positions. Students will practice more advanced analytical and representational techniques, including analogue and digital modelling and simulation of landscape processes (eg. GIS, BIM, etc). Coursework may be conducted in relation to real-life projects (urban or rural landscape sites) to offer students first-hand design-research and material fabrication experience. Thesis Studio is self-directed, and the topic of the thesis project is expected to be preliminarily developed in discussion with instructors in this course.

title: Landscape Architecture Design Studio IV Thesis
requirements: For students of MSc in Landscape Architecture.
description: The concluding studio comprises an integrated design thesis project elaborated from topics defined in LARC6111. As a capstone project, students are expected to develop their sustainable design thesis through in-depth research and analysis to synthesise accomplished landscape proposals that address multi-faceted concerns (ecological, social, political, economic) through multi-scalar designs (from regional strategy to local interventions). Self-directed thesis projects should explore innovative topics (eg. regenerative design, biophilia, nature-based low-carbon solutions, environmental justice, etc.), and aspire to resolving technically complex sustainable landscape designs that balance human needs while enhancing urban-rural landscape systems and ecological processes.

title: Professional Practice and Management in Landscape Architecture
requirements: For students of MSc in Landscape Architecture.
description: This course introduces students to the professional practice of landscape architecture. Regulatory control mechanisms and significant procedures for land use, planning and design development in Hong Kong will be discussed. Codes of professional conduct, nature of scope of services, project team members and roles, project management practices and will be presented. Tender documents, specifications and construction contracts, as well as the administration process for implementation of landscape works will be discussed; while related legal aspects in the Laws of Tort; Contract; Land; and Environment will be mentioned. In addition, the course covers professional presentations and communication with client and user communities while advocating for values of diversity of sustainable design practices and environmental stewardship in compliance with UN SDGs.
